16.1: The divine qualities begin: fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and yoga, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study, austerity, uprightness.
16.2: Non-injury, truth, absence of anger, renunciation, tranquillity, absence of slander, compassion, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, absence of fickleness.
16.3: Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice and from pride — these belong to one born to a divine state.
16.4: The demonic qualities: hypocrisy, arrogance, self-conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance.
16.5: The divine qualities lead to liberation, the demonic to bondage; do not grieve — you are born with the divine ones.
16.6: There are two kinds of beings in this world, the divine and the demonic; the divine have been described at length, now hear of the other.
16.7: The demonic know neither right action nor right abstention; in them there is no purity, no good conduct, no truth.
16.8: The demonic say the world is without truth, without moral basis, without God, caused by lust alone.
16.9: Holding this view, these lost souls of small intellect and cruel deeds arise as enemies of the world for its destruction.
16.10: Filled with insatiable desire, full of hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, holding false views through delusion, they act with impure resolve.
16.11: Beset by immeasurable anxiety ending only in death, regarding gratification of desire as the highest aim, convinced that is all there is.
16.12: Bound by a hundred ties of hope, given over to lust and anger, they strive to amass wealth unlawfully for sense enjoyment.
16.13: 'This I have gained today, that desire I shall obtain; this wealth is mine and more shall be mine.'
16.14: 'That enemy I have slain and others I shall slay; I am the lord, the enjoyer, successful, powerful and happy.'
16.15: 'I am wealthy and well-born — who is equal to me? I shall sacrifice, I shall give, I shall rejoice' — thus deluded by ignorance.
16.16: Bewildered by many thoughts, entangled in the net of delusion, addicted to sense pleasures, they fall into a foul hell.
16.17: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy.
16.18: Given to egoism, power, insolence, lust and anger, these malicious people hate Me in their own and others' bodies.
16.19: These cruel haters, worst among men, I hurl repeatedly into demonic wombs in the cycles of rebirth.
16.20: Entering demonic wombs birth after birth, deluded, they never reach Me and sink to the lowest state.
16.21: The famous triple gate of hell, destructive of the self: lust, anger and greed — therefore abandon these three.
16.22: Freed from these three gates of darkness, one works out one's own good and reaches the supreme goal.
16.23: One who casts aside the scriptural injunction and acts on impulse attains neither perfection nor happiness nor the highest goal.
16.24: Therefore let scripture be your authority in deciding what should and should not be done; knowing what it prescribes, act accordingly.
